chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: The Amsterdam News article of 1940 and Harlem at that moment
summary: Willard reads a 1940 Amsterdam News piece about Spikes's chair and songs alongside Harlem nightclub news.

bands.name: Louis Jordan and His Decca Recording Orchestra

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You brought out a...one page of The Amsterdam News from Saturday, September 21, 1940, showing you sitting on one of the hydraulic chairs...
...uh, bootblack chairs, and this is apparently an interview done when you were in New York representing them...

And there's an article on--I think it's Page 20. It's hard to tell because the page number is missing from this sheet but Page 19's on the other side--and there's an article here about you and your brothers and your musical careers and your brother's inventions, and it's very nice. And this is simultaneous with...it's interesting that...the things that were going on at the same time. When you were in New York representing the bootblack chair, uh, the Elks Rendezvous, "Harlem's finest nightclub" was presenting Willie Bryant, Allen Drew, Flash & Dash, it says, and music by Louis Jordan And His Decca Recording Orchestra...
...and at Small's Paradise, Jimmie Mordecai was M.C., and Maurice Hubbard's Orchestra was appearing, and according to
Dan Burley's column, uh..."Billie Holiday may work with Art Tatum at Cafe Society down in the Village" and...uh...news about Pigmeat Markham...

Let's see, what else was going on...it's... it says, "From the number of offers Cab Calloway has received to star in Broadway shows, every indication points to a healthy representation of colored performers in the New York legitimate field for the forthcoming season," and

"Calloway several months ago" received an offer from Al Lewis, a producer, to star in a production of "Little Joe." And then it tells all the people that recorded "Someday Sweetheart" here in the article about you--Bing Crosby, Ethel Waters, Alberta Hunter. The Spikes brothers, B.F. and John C. also wrote oldtime favorites as...such oldtime favorites as 'Some Rainy Day,' 'Old Fashioned Mother,' 'Smiling With A Broken Heart,' and 'You're Not the Only One That's Lonesome'.
